extracted.intended_audience: Program sponsors, Registration Agencies, State CTE Agencies, intermediaries, participating employers, educational institutions, and legal/compliance staff involved with registered CTE apprenticeship programs
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and quality standards for establishing, operating, reviewing, deregistering, and reinstating Career and Technical Education (CTE) registered apprenticeship programs under the Department of Labor rules. Includes required program standards, application materials, compliance and hearing procedures, and responsibilities of sponsors, Registration Agencies, and State CTE Agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor cooperation with program reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors and participating employers are required to cooperate with requests for interviews or documentation from the Registration Agency and must not impede the Agency's ability to interview prospective, current, or former apprentices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration Agencies may consider all relevant information and data in program reviews and must review program performance under §29.25(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Program Review Findings content
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon completion of a program review, the Registration Agency must present a written Notice of Program Review Findings to the sponsor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If review indicates noncompliance, the notice must include: (1) identified deficiency(ies); (2) how to cure/remedy them; (3) requirement to develop and submit a compliance action plan pursuant to §29.19(f); and (4) a statement that administrative actions in §29.20 may be undertaken if compliance is not achieved within the required timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance action plan timing and rebuttal
rubrics_metrics.description: When sponsor receives a Notice of Program Review Findings indicating failure to comply, the sponsor must within 45 calendar days either submit a compliance action plan that meets specified requirements or submit a written rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration Agencies may extend this deadline one time by up to 45 days for good cause upon sponsor request; if Agency upholds findings after rebuttal, sponsor then has 45 calendar days to submit an approved compliance action plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance action plan required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A compliance action plan must include: (i) a specific written commitment to correct/remediate identified deficiencies; (ii) the precise actions to be taken for each deficiency; (iii) the time period within which each cited deficiency will be remedied and corrective changes implemented; and (iv) the name of the individual(s) responsible for correcting each deficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration Agency will evaluate the plan and choose to approve and terminate review, approve and continue review until implementation, or reject and work to revise or initiate deregistration under §29.20.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration Agency responses to compliance plans
rubrics_metrics.description: After evaluating a sponsor's compliance action plan, the Registration Agency must elect one of three responses: (1) approve and determine program is in compliance and terminate review; (2) approve but continue review until plan is implemented; or (3) reject and either work with sponsor to revise plan or initiate deregistration under §29.20.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds and options for deregistration
rubrics_metrics.description: A Registration Agency may deregister a program when it determines the sponsor or participating employer is not operating in accordance with this part (or part 30) and the program has failed to correct violations or failed to submit/implement an approved compliance action plan within required timeframes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before deregistration the Agency may offer technical assistance, require a compliance action plan, suspend sponsor's right to register new apprentices, or proceed to deregister the program pursuant to §29.20.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary deregistration requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A program sponsor may request voluntary deregistration in writing; the Registration Agency will deregister and provide written confirmation after receiving the request that includes an effective date and a statement that the sponsor will notify all apprentices within 15 calendar days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsor's notice to apprentices must state: (i) that sponsor requested deregistration and the effective date; (ii) that deregistration deprives the apprentice of individual registration; (iii) that deregistration removes the apprentice from coverage for Federal purposes; and (iv) that the apprentice will be referred to the Registration Agency for transfer information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of deregistration by Administrator
rubrics_metrics.description: A former sponsor may request review by the Administrator by submitting an electronic written request within 30 calendar days of the Notice of Deregistration, including any additional relevant facts or documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If SAA issued Notice, sponsor must simultaneously furnish copy to Administrator; SAA must transmit to Administrator within 15 days copies of records with pertinent facts. Administrator may request additional information and will issue a final decision as quickly as practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to hearing and limits on hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Except where deregistration is based on failure to respond to contact attempts or failure to register at least one apprentice, a sponsor may request a hearing before the Office of Administrative Law Judges (OALJ) within 15 calendar days of receipt of the Administrator's final decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If SAA is Registration Agency, sponsor must request Administrator review before requesting an OALJ hearing. Where basis is non-response or failure to register apprentices, Administrator's decision is final and no OALJ hearing is permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing procedures and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Hearings on deregistration are governed by part 18 procedures with specified modifications: ALJ receives documentary evidence and makes it part of the record; technical rules of evidence do not apply but principles to assure credible evidence and cross-examination will be used; ALJ may authorize limited discovery; ALJ must issue a written decision within 90 calendar days of close of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ALJ will uphold Administrator's decision unless sponsor shows it was arbitrary, capricious, an abuse of discretion, or not in accordance with law; parties may petition ARB within 15 days; ARB may accept for review within 30 days and must decide within 180 days of close of record if accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of program registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Any apprenticeship program deregistered under §29.20 may be reinstated at any time upon presentation of adequate evidence to the Registration Agency that the apprenticeship program is operating in accordance with this part and part 30.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions request and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for exemption from any provision of this subpart must be made in writing to the Administrator and must contain a statement of reasons supporting the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrator may grant exemptions only for good cause and may not grant exemptions with respect to requirements set forth outside this subpart, including other Federal, State, or local laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination between Registration Agency and State CTE Agency
rubrics_metrics.description: The Registration Agency and State CTE Agency must coordinate on the overall administration of registered CTE apprenticeship programs, including approvals, program reviews, data collection, technical assistance, and compliance activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordination ensures both parties work cooperatively to support LEAs, IHEs, and intermediaries while ensuring programs meet requirements; nothing alters existing State CTE authorities or Registration Agency oversight; SAA must include written agreement as part of State Apprenticeship Plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written agreement for Statewide coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: The State CTE Agency and Registration Agency must enter into a written agreement for Statewide coordination and operation of registered CTE apprenticeship programs describing roles and responsibilities of each agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An SAA must include such an agreement in its State Apprenticeship Plan to establish registered CTE apprenticeship programs in the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry skills framework approval criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: An industry skills framework will be approved if it: (i) provides structure for professional behaviors, workplace competencies, and theoretical knowledge; (ii) describes skills validated by industry as nationally applicable and widely recognized; (iii) describes skills specified in an OJT outline and obtained through attainment of at least 900 hours of OJT; (iv) aligns with a CTE program approved by State CTE Agency; and (v) details industry-validated methods for ongoing evaluations to assess competency attainment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrator oversees development and updates of industry-validated, portable, rigorous frameworks to be used by States and sponsors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment and decision timeline for frameworks
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrator will solicit public comment for at least 30 days on each new or updated industry skills framework; determination will be made within 90 days of submission for public comment, subject to possible extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrator may consider data and other relevant information and will maintain a public list of frameworks and decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards must include OJT outline aligned with framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Each registered CTE apprenticeship program must have written standards that include an on-the-job training outline that aligns with an approved industry skills framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards must include CTE apprenticeship-related instruction description
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must describe the CTE apprenticeship-related instruction including: it must be at least 540 hours in duration; result in at least 12 postsecondary credit hours; and lead to proficiency in skills/competencies described in the industry skills framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Description must include whether time in instruction counts as hours worked and, if so, wage rate and fringe benefits for those hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards must list recognized postsecondary credits/credentials
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must describe recognized postsecondary credit hours and credentials awarded, including any associate or baccalaureate degree associated with the program and the name of issuing entity(ies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards must describe pathways from CTE apprenticeship completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must describe how completion of the program will result in selection into an apprenticeship registered under subpart A, enrollment in a postsecondary educational program, or employment, including any advanced standing granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: OJT duration and proficiency requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must describe the employment in which CTE apprentices will be employed for on-the-job training: on-the-job training must be a minimum of 900 hours in duration and lead to proficiency in the skills and competencies described in the industry skills framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wage requirements for CTE apprentices
rubrics_metrics.description: CTE apprentices must be paid a progressively increasing schedule of wages consistent with industry skills and competencies; the entry wage must be at least the minimum wage under the Fair Labor Standards Act unless a higher wage is required by other applicable law or collective bargaining agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required apprentice-to-journeyworker ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must specify the program's numeric ratio of CTE apprentices to journeyworkers that is consistent with proper safety, health, supervision, and training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ratio must be consistent with any applicable collective bargaining agreements and Federal/State laws, and must be specific and clearly described as to application to workforce, workplace, worksite, job site, department, or plant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probationary period limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must include a probationary period that may not exceed 30 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation of adequate facilities and equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor must attest, supported by available documentation, that the program will provide adequate, safe, and accessible facilities and equipment for training and supervision of CTE apprentices compliant with all applicable Federal, State, and local disability, occupational safety, and occupational health laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation of adequate safety training
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor must attest that the program will provide adequate, industry-recognized safety training for CTE apprentices on the job and in CTE apprenticeship-related instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum qualifications for entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must state any minimum qualifications required by a sponsor and its participating employers for persons entering the registered CTE apprenticeship program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor selection procedures must comply with part 30
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must include the sponsor's procedures for the selection of CTE apprentices, which must comply with the requirements for selection of apprentices set forth in part 30 of this title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive services listing
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must include a list of supportive services that may be available to the CTE apprentice during their registered CTE apprenticeship program, including whether services are provided by the sponsor or partner organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include childcare, transportation, equipment, tools, or other services to address participation/completion barriers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced standing/prior learning credit process
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must describe the process by which the sponsor will reduce the usual term of OJT or instruction due to a registered CTE apprentice's prior learning, training, or experience, or accelerated progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process must be fair, transparent, equitable, objectively identify/assess/document prior learning, and result in advanced standing or credit and an increased wage commensurate with progression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trainer and instructor qualifications documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must include documentation that the qualifications and experience of trainers and instructors providing OJT and CTE apprenticeship-related instruction satisfy the requirements of §29.12.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of Registration Agency and State CTE Agency in standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must identify the Registration Agency and the State CTE Agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor equal opportunity pledge and attestation
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must include the sponsor's equal opportunity pledge pursuant to §30.3(c) and an attestation that the program will be operated in accordance with part 30 and, where applicable, an approved State EEO plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information for complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must include contact information (name, address, telephone number, and email) for the appropriate individual with authority under the program to receive, process, and make disposition of complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible sponsor organization types
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible sponsors for registered CTE apprenticeship programs include: LEAs eligible under Perkins; institutions of higher education as defined under Perkins; State CTE Agencies or other State agencies sharing CTE responsibility; and intermediary organizations designated by State CTE Agency, SEA, LEA, or IHE with expertise in organizing/coordinating registered CTE apprenticeship programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intermediary examples: local labor org affiliates, employers, trade/industry orgs, local workforce boards, IHEs, LEAs, or other public/private/non-profit entities experienced with Perkins funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor application required materials
rubrics_metrics.description: To apply for registration, prospective program sponsors must electronically submit an application that includes: (i) OJT outline aligned with an associated industry skills framework; (ii) a CTE apprenticeship-related instruction outline; (iii) standards of registered CTE apprenticeship for the proposed program; (iv) the CTE apprenticeship agreement; and (v) a written plan containing specified elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application must also include assurances regarding formalized commitments (MOUs) among partners and maintenance of records necessary to determine compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written plan: diversity and inclusion of selected students
rubrics_metrics.description: Written plan must describe how the program will ensure selected students reflect a diverse and inclusive cross-section of current student body enrollment of participating secondary or postsecondary schools consistent with part 30 requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written plan: alignment with approved industry skills framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Written plan must describe how the CTE program's training and curriculum align with an approved industry skills framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written plan: credits/credentials description and usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Written plan must describe secondary credits or recognized postsecondary credit hours and credentials the program may provide, including how the program confers such credits/credentials and their usefulness for entry into employment, registered apprenticeship under subpart A, or postsecondary education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written plan: employer workplace safety/inclusivity description
rubrics_metrics.description: Written plan must describe how the sponsor will ensure each employer has an established record of maintaining a safe and inclusive workplace free from discrimination, violence, harassment, intimidation, and retaliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written plan: access to career services and supportive services
rubrics_metrics.description: Written plan must describe how CTE apprentices will have access to a broad range of career services and supportive services that enable participation in, and successful completion of, the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive services may include childcare, transportation, equipment, tools, or other supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written plan: routine monitoring and oversight by sponsor
rubrics_metrics.description: Written plan must describe the routine monitoring and oversight conducted by the sponsor of all aspects of the registered CTE apprenticeship program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written plan: affirmative steps to provide EEO
rubrics_metrics.description: Written plan must describe how the sponsor will implement upon registration the affirmative steps to provide equal employment opportunity required by §30.3(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At minimum the description must: (1) identify individual(s) responsible for overseeing EEO commitment; (2) identify publications/documents and locations where EEO pledge will be published/posted; (3) describe schedule for orientation/info sessions for administration/operation participants (including apprentices and journeyworkers) about EEO policy; (4) provide list of current recruitment sources generating referrals from all demographic groups, with contacts; and (5) describe procedures to ensure apprentices are not harassed/discriminated against and include anti-harassment training schedule/content source and complaint handling/resolution procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assurance of formalized partner commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor must provide an assurance that specific commitments, roles, and responsibilities of employers, schools, LEAs, postsecondary institutions, intermediaries, and others are formalized through memoranda of understanding or other written agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assurance to maintain required records
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor must assure that it will maintain any required records that the Registration Agency considers necessary to determine compliance with this part and applicable Federal/State laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent with §29.18.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intermediary sponsor additional responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: If an intermediary serves as sponsor, it must ensure compliance with this subpart and coordinate with relevant LEAs, schools, postsecondary institutions, community colleges, or CTE providers to ensure all requirements (and any additional State requirements) are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor standards adoption agreement: employer obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Each participating employer under a sponsor standards adoption agreement must: (A) adopt and comply with sponsor's standards of registered CTE apprenticeship; (B) comply with all other applicable requirements of this part; and (C) cooperate with and provide assistance to the program sponsor, including providing any apprenticeship-related data and records necessary to assess compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission of executed adoption agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each executed sponsor standards adoption agreement must be transmitted to the Registration Agency by the program sponsor within 30 days of execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension/cancellation of adoption agreements and sponsor duties
rubrics_metrics.description: A sponsor standards adoption agreement may be canceled by employer with 30 days' written notice; sponsor must suspend or cancel the agreement if it determines the employer failed to satisfy provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsor must provide written notice of suspension/cancellation to the participating employer, affected CTE apprentices, and Registration Agency explaining reason; if cancellation interrupts training, sponsor must make reasonable efforts to place apprentices with another participating employer; Registration Agency may initiate deregistration if sponsor fails to suspend/cancel as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: CTE apprenticeship agreement signatures and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: All registered CTE programs must develop a written CTE apprenticeship agreement signed prior to start by the CTE apprentice, the apprentice's parent/guardian if under 18, the program sponsor, the secondary or postsecondary institution in which the apprentice is enrolled, and any participating employers who adopted the sponsor's standards adoption agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of the signed agreement and program standards must be given to the apprentice (and parent/guardian if applicable) prior to start date.

rubrics_metrics.name: CTE apprenticeship agreement: identification and privacy info
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement must include contact and identifying information for the apprentice, including date of birth and, on a voluntary basis, Social Security number.

rubrics_metrics.name: CTE apprenticeship agreement: program/contact documents incorporation
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement must include contact information for Registration Agency, sponsor, participating employers; identification of job/occupation and copies of associated industry skills framework and instruction outline; and incorporation, directly or by reference, of the program's standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: CTE apprenticeship agreement: roles, duties, and rights information
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement must describe respective roles, duties, and responsibilities of apprentice, sponsor, and participating employer, including providing apprentices information about their rights and protections under Federal, State, and local laws and the process for filing complaints with Registration Agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: CTE apprenticeship agreement: term and probation
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement must specify the term of the apprenticeship including start date, expected duration, OJT start date, and a probationary period not exceeding 30 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: CTE apprenticeship agreement: wages and hours disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement must state detailed entry wage and subsequent graduated wage scale; disclose expected minimum hours allocated to OJT and instruction components; and describe whether instruction time is paid and, if so, wage rate and whether instruction occurs during work hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: CTE apprenticeship agreement: competency measurement and supports
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement must describe methods used to measure progress on competency attainment and describe any supportive services available (childcare, transportation, equipment, tools, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: CTE apprenticeship agreement: costs, credentials, dispute authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement must state any unreimbursed costs apprentices may incur, describe secondary/postsecondary credits or credentials awarded upon completion, include a statement parties will adhere to part 30, and provide contact info for the authority to receive/resolve disputes that cannot be locally resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: CTE apprenticeship agreement: consent for disclosure by institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement must include consent from the apprentice (or parent/guardian if under 18 and not in postsecondary institution) permitting the institution to disclose individual apprentice-level information to program sponsor, intermediary-designating entity, participating employers, Registration Agency, Department, and other institutions involved in administering program as required under subpart B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibitions on non-compete and restrictive provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A sponsor or participating employer cannot include in the CTE apprenticeship agreement or otherwise impose a non-compete or other provision that restricts an apprentice's labor market mobility or ability to seek employment with another employer prior to program completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on non-disclosure provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor or participating employer cannot include NDAs that prevent the worker from working in same field after employment or that restrict an apprentice's ability to file a complaint with a Registration Agency or governmental body concerning possible violations; NDAs protecting confidential commercial information or trade secrets are permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission timing for executed CTE apprenticeship agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Program sponsor must submit a completed copy of the executed CTE apprenticeship agreement for each registered CTE apprentice to the Registration Agency within 30 days of execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of completion issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: CTE apprentices who meet the CTE apprenticeship-related instruction and the OJT outlined in the industry skills framework will receive a certificate of completion of registered CTE apprenticeship from the Registration Agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration Agency application review timeline and notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration Agency must review a sponsor's application and provide a determination on eligibility for registration within 90 days of receipt of a complete application and inform applicants in writing of all decisions; if denied, Agency must explain reasons in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration Agency obligation to provide technical assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Registration Agency is responsible for providing outreach, technical assistance, and other services to potential sponsors, participating employers, and partners to support adoption of registered CTE apprenticeship and ensure compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint investigations and anti-retaliation applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaint investigation and anti-retaliation provisions in §29.17 apply to this subpart, except that a Registration Agency may refer complaints under this subsection to the State CTE Agency as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program reviews coordination and non-impact on Perkins funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Program reviews for CTE apprenticeship should follow §29.19 processes and be coordinated with the relevant State CTE Agency; the result of any program review will not impact an entity's eligibility for Perkins funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of deregistration, hearings, and reinstatement processes
rubrics_metrics.description: The deregistration process (§29.20), hearings on deregistration (§29.21), and reinstatement process (§29.22) described earlier apply to Subpart B CTE apprenticeship programs.
